understanding: An execution task refining an in-progress webcam upgrade for the OKO project. Three concrete deliverables: (1) set the default model in configs/live-webcam.yaml to yolo11m (currently yolov8n) without hardcoding yolo11x, keeping the model config-driven via model_file; (2) add conf_threshold (default 0.4) to DetectorConfig (src/oko/config/schema.py) and actually apply it in UltralyticsDetector — note the factory at factory.py:26 currently constructs UltralyticsDetector(model_file=...) and silently drops the existing confidence param, so the wiring must be fixed; (3) perform a single yolo11x run on real device 0, saving runs/webcam-proof-v2.png plus a structured detection log (class+confidence). The default must stay yolo11m; yolo11x is a one-off quality-ceiling demo only.
summary: Edit live-webcam.yaml so the default resolves to yolo11m (model_file: models/yolo11m.pt, model_size: m); add conf_threshold: float = 0.4 to DetectorConfig and wire it through the factory into UltralyticsDetector's predict(conf=...) (fixing the dropped-confidence bug); then run yolo11x ONCE on device 0 via a one-off override (CLI flag/temp config), reusing the existing v1 capture path to write an annotated runs/webcam-proof-v2.png and a class+confidence log. Keep tests green and ensure the new default weight is fetchable/present so the balanced default is actually runnable.

decision_atoms.statement: Set the default by pointing model_file at models/yolo11m.pt (with model_size: m, model_family: yolo) in configs/live-webcam.yaml, not by introducing a new hardcoded model constant.
decision_atoms.reason: UltralyticsDetector and build_detector resolve the weight purely from config.model_file (no version baked in); changing the YAML keeps the model configurable and overridable, satisfying both the 'yolo11m default' and 'must remain configurable' success tests with one edit.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: yolo11m.pt (~40MB) is not in models/ yet (only yolov8n.pt), so the default is not runnable until the weight is fetched; readiness checks that validate file presence will fail until then.

decision_atoms.statement: Add conf_threshold: float = 0.4 to DetectorConfig and pass it through the factory as UltralyticsDetector(model_file=..., confidence=config.conf_threshold), keeping the detector's internal param name 'confidence'.
decision_atoms.reason: The detector already accepts confidence and feeds it to predict(conf=...); the only real gap is factory.py:26 dropping it. Mapping conf_threshold->confidence at the factory is the lowest-churn fix that makes the threshold actually apply at detection time, satisfying the 'utilize conf_threshold during detection' test.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A name mismatch (conf_threshold in config vs confidence in the detector) remains; clearer would be renaming the detector param, but that touches tests/constructors for marginal benefit.

decision_atoms.statement: Run yolo11x exactly once via a one-off override (a CLI --model-file flag or a throwaway temp config), never by editing the committed default.
decision_atoms.reason: Directly satisfies 'do not hardcode yolo11x' and 'demo run performed only once' while still producing the requested quality-ceiling proof; the committed config stays at yolo11m.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The current webcam.py entrypoint has no model-override flag and does not save annotated images, so either a small flag is added or the existing v1 capture script is parameterized — minor extra code.

decision_atoms.statement: Produce runs/webcam-proof-v2.png as an annotated frame (boxes+labels via ultralytics result.plot()) plus a sidecar log mirroring the existing runs/webcam-proof-capture.json format (class, confidence, bbox, model, device, latency).
decision_atoms.reason: A v1 proof flow already exists (webcam-proof.png + webcam-proof-capture.json); matching that shape keeps the deliverable consistent and gives the user both a visual proof and the structured class+confidence log required by the output_format.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Reusing/extending the existing capture script requires locating it (not webcam.py itself); a clean reusable --save-annotated path is slightly more work than an ad-hoc one-shot.

decision_atoms.statement: Add a unit test asserting the configured conf_threshold flows into the predict call, and rely on existing default values to keep current DetectorConfig constructions valid.
decision_atoms.reason: Existing tests (test_providers, test_live_readiness) build DetectorConfig without a threshold; a default of 0.4 keeps them passing, and a focused test prevents silent regressions of the dropped-confidence bug recurring.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slightly more test surface; but without it the wiring fix is unguarded and could silently break again.

assumptions: ultralytics and opencv (cv2) are installed in this environment (supported by runs/live-extras-install.txt and runs/webcam-real-run.txt from the prior real run); the dep-version check needed approval and was not confirmed live.
Device 0 is a real, working webcam — the existing runs/webcam-proof.png (v1) implies a successful prior capture on device 0.
Network access is available so ultralytics can auto-download yolo11x.pt (~110MB) and yolo11m.pt (~40MB) on first load, or the weights can be pre-fetched into models/.
'Log of detections' means a machine-readable sidecar file (JSON/text) with class+confidence per object, like the v1 webcam-proof-capture.json, in addition to being echoed in the final JSON output.
The scene in front of device 0 contains recognizable COCO objects (e.g. a person) so 'good recognition' is demonstrable; detection quality is scene-dependent and cannot be guaranteed by code alone.
There is an existing capture/annotation script behind v1 that can be parameterized; if not, adding a small one-off capture step is within the allowed low complexity.
model_size/model_family in the config are descriptive metadata; the effective weight is whatever model_file points to.

risks.risk: yolo11x.pt / yolo11m.pt weights are absent (only yolov8n.pt present) and the environment is offline or download-restricted, so the demo run and/or the new default cannot load.
risks.mitigation: Pre-fetch both weights into models/ and verify on disk before running; fail fast with a clear message if download is blocked; confirm the readiness check passes for the new yolo11m default.

risks.risk: Physical camera at device 0 is unavailable/busy at run time, so the one-shot yolo11x capture fails and no real frame can be returned.
risks.mitigation: Verify camera availability first (the v1 proof confirms it worked before); ensure no other process holds the device; capture is read-only and retried only within the single permitted run.

risks.risk: conf_threshold is added to config but not actually applied because the factory keeps dropping it (current factory.py:26 ignores confidence), making the success test pass nominally while detection still uses the 0.25 default.
risks.mitigation: Wire config.conf_threshold through build_detector into the constructor and assert via a unit test that predict receives conf=0.4.

risks.risk: 'Good recognition' is subjective and scene-dependent; a sparse or poorly-lit frame yields a weak proof even with yolo11x.
risks.mitigation: Stage a clear subject (person/common objects) in good lighting; apply conf 0.4 to suppress noise; include the full class+confidence log so quality is evidenced quantitatively.

risks.risk: DetectorConfig uses extra='forbid'; a config carrying conf_threshold against an un-updated schema (or stale checkout) raises a validation error.
risks.mitigation: Land the schema field and the config edit together; conf_threshold remains optional with default 0.4 so existing configs without it still validate.

risks.risk: Switching the committed default from yolov8n to yolo11m changes runtime behavior/perf for anyone relying on the old default.
risks.mitigation: This is the explicitly requested balanced default; document the change in PROGRESS.md and keep the model fully overridable via model_file.

minimal_version: 1) In configs/live-webcam.yaml set model_family: yolo, model_size: m, model_file: models/yolo11m.pt. 2) In src/oko/config/schema.py add conf_threshold: float = 0.4 to DetectorConfig. 3) In src/oko/providers/factory.py change the ultralytics branch to UltralyticsDetector(model_file=config.model_file, confidence=config.conf_threshold) so the threshold actually applies. 4) Ensure models/yolo11m.pt is present (fetch if missing) so the default is runnable. 5) Run yolo11x ONCE on device 0 via a temp override config or CLI flag (committed default stays yolo11m), capture an annotated runs/webcam-proof-v2.png plus a class+confidence detection log, reusing the v1 capture path. 6) Run the existing test suite to confirm green. Return the real frame path and the detection log.
advanced_version: All of minimal, plus: rename the detector param to conf_threshold (with back-compat) so config and code agree; add a unit test asserting conf=config.conf_threshold is passed to predict; emit a richer structured log (class, confidence, bbox, model, device, latency_ms, timestamp) matching/extending webcam-proof-capture.json; add reproducible CLI flags to src/oko/live/webcam.py (--model-file override and --save-annotated <path>) and a small annotate-and-save helper using result.plot(), so future proof runs need no temp configs; pre-fetch yolo11m/yolo11x into models/ and gitignore large weights; strengthen LiveReadinessChecker to validate weight presence with an actionable message; and record the default change and the v2 proof in PROGRESS.md.
